title: Mean community direction scores remained negative after a sampling correction in four US trawl samples in 1982-2019
abstract: We tested whether annual changes in recorded marine communities tend to reverse direction. Adjacent changes share a survey year, which can create a negative direction score through sampling error. We derived a finite-sample correction under independent haul sampling assumptions. Mean corrected scores were -1.15, -1.30, -1.56 and -1.85 in eastern Bering Sea and Northeast US fall samples in two periods from 1982 to 2019. All four adjusted mean intervals were below zero. The correction removed 34-78 percent of the magnitude of direct negative means. A positive link to the product of successive seasonal temperature changes was clear only in early Northeast records. Increasing the modeled correction by 50 percent changed the sign of both Northeast means. Thus the sampling assumptions are material. This result does not prove ecological cycles or a causal climate effect. Spatial dependence, detection, gear, short series and coarse surface temperature limit inference. The package gives a proof, exact enumeration checks, raw source hashes, a full raw rebuild check, code, derived data and a figure.

display.caption: Left: direct and corrected mean direction scores. Right: slopes against the product of successive seasonal temperature changes. Intervals use separate four-test adjustments for means and slopes. Negative means do not prove ecological cycles.

citations.reason: Source of verified published incidence tables, haul denominators, seasonal climate evidence and raw build code. We rebuilt inputs from shared raw files. Our adjacent-change score and tests differ; raw observations overlap.
Prior marine heatwave and fish community study motivates the variability question. Our seasonal measure does not test heatwaves.
